title: Simulation of a loop-body call
statement: Let $B$ and $F$ be finite Boolean Turing machines, let $a$ be a state of $B$, and choose Boolean parameters for find mode and startup. For an input word $x$, an initial configuration $c$ of $B$, a release flag, a time $t$, a Boolean word $w$, and a configuration of $F$ used as fuel, assume that $c$ is not halted, every configuration reached from $c$ in fewer than $t$ steps is not halted, and none of those configurations is in state $a$ except possibly at time $0$ when the release flag is true. Then after $t$ steps the constructed host machine, started in the encoded call configuration, is in the encoded call configuration for the body machine after $t$ steps; its release flag is the original one exactly when $t=0$, and its additional flag is true exactly when the body configuration at time $t$ is halted. The word and fuel configuration are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: finite Boolean machines $B,F$ and anchor state of $B$
input word and initial configuration of $B$
Boolean word $w$ and fuel configuration of $F$
initial body configuration is not halted
all body configurations at times $u<t$ are not halted
before time $t$, the anchor state occurs only at time zero when release is true
caveat: The host machine and encoded call configuration are given by lengthy private constructions, so their full operational meaning cannot be stated briefly without reproducing those constructions.
